notes:
Board tab as a review surface (epic CHR-618). Interaction rules for implementation:

**Filter ∪ pins.** One filter, shared by the sidebar's screen list and the Board tab (ephemeral per-project state in the daemon, not per-screen data). The Board tile grid shows exactly the union of screens matching the active filter and screens the human has pinned. The filter input itself lives only in the sidebar (decision `chr621-filter-lives-in-sidebar`) — DECIDED. The Board's own toolbar has no filter field, only a `status` readout of the result ("N shown — M matches · K pinned").

**Zoom — continuous slider, 5%–200%.** DECIDED, replacing the original preset-only design after Christian rejected it: `$board-toolbar` embeds `$zoom-slider`, range **5%** (floor) to 200% (ceiling), linear mapping. CORRECTED (implementation measurement): the floor was originally set to 10% in the design, based on this design's 180px mock tiles; measured against Christian's real ~186-screen project with real 390×844 tiles, the true fit-all scale is ~7.6%, so a 10% floor would have clipped his own requirement that Fit all show the whole project. The floor moved to 5% to leave headroom below the measured value. The −/+ step buttons move the value by a fixed step; dragging the thumb sets it continuously. Ctrl/Cmd+scroll-wheel over the canvas and pinch-to-zoom (trackpad/touch) move this exact same value, not a separate control. `Fit all` is a one-shot action, not a toggle. `100%` is a plain jump-to-value shortcut. Neither quick-jump button is "active" unless the slider's current value exactly matches it. Zoom level (like the edge toggle) is a **browser-local UI preference** — not daemon state, not agent-settable, and it **persists per browser/session**.

**The board grid is viewport-shaped, not a fixed mock layout.** DECIDED (implementation measurement): the real board's column/row count is computed from the current tile list and the board's actual surface area so that "Fit all" uses the viewport best — this is recomputed on screen-list change, on window resize, and on project switch, but NEVER while the human is actively zooming (the grid shape doesn't reflow mid-drag). This project's design screens (`board-view-zoomed-out` etc.) use a simplified fixed-size 180px mock tile in a fixed 1440×900 frame for illustration — their specific percentages (e.g. 42%) are mock arithmetic, not the real numbers; see each screen's own notes.

**Any new low-zoom screen must be arithmetically honest** (within this design file's own simplified mock terms — the design's 180px tile and fixed frame, not the real app's 390×844 tiles or its dynamic viewport). DECIDED, the hard way — `board-view-zoomed-out` was rejected for showing a "Fit all" zoom % that didn't match how much of the canvas its tiles actually filled. Compute it: `zoom = mini_tile_width ÷ native_tile_width (180px)`, choose a column/row grid whose footprint at that tile size fills the board's usable canvas area, and set the toolbar's readout/slider-thumb to that computed value. See `board-view-zoomed-out`'s screen notes for the full worked arithmetic (186 tiles, 17×11 grid, 76×63px tiles → 42% in mock terms; ~7.6% is the measured real-world figure).

**Label degradation by zoom.** Below ~60% zoom, tile name labels hide entirely (`typography.size-xs` scales under ~8px there, illegible). From ~60% to 100%, labels show truncated with an ellipsis if they overflow the tile width. At 100% and above, the full name always shows.

**Pin / unpin — visible affordance vs. overview noise.** At normal (≥60%) zoom, a `$pin-button` instance sits on every visible tile (top-right corner) and every visible sidebar row — always rendered, in whichever state is correct, not hover-only; see `board-view`/`board-view-presented`. **Below the same ~60% legibility threshold that hides labels, the UNPINNED affordance is not rendered at all** — it is hover-revealed on a tile at low zoom instead, and a static design cannot show a hover state, so low-zoom reference screens simply omit the unfilled marker rather than fake one. **Pinned markers always render, at every zoom**, since a filled `$pin-button` carries information (this screen is on the board because it's pinned) that a hover can't substitute for — see `board-view-zoomed-out`, where only its 5 actually-pinned tiles (of 186) carry a marker. `default` (unpinned) = grey outline, muted monochrome SVG pin icon, shown only at ≥60% zoom; `pinned` = accent-filled, white icon, shown at any zoom. The `pinned` variant is also the sole marker distinguishing "here via pin" from "here via match."

**Pinned-but-not-matching distinguishability.** DECIDED — `$board-tile`'s `outside-filter` variant (dashed accent border + a `$tag-chip` `badge` reading "pinned · outside filter") is the final treatment. Applies only to tiles on the board solely because they're pinned; a matching tile (pinned or not) uses `$board-tile` `default`.

**Clear pins.** DECIDED — no confirmation dialog. A `$btn` (default variant) labelled "Clear pins" in the toolbar's `actions` slot, shown only when the pinned count is non-zero.

**Agent-presented indicator.** DECIDED — stays visible until the human dismisses it (✕), no auto-dismiss timer. A single dismissible pill banner positioned inside the canvas, clearly below the toolbar — "Agent switched you here to show N screens."

See screens `board-view` (canonical: filter+pins+toolbar+clear-pins at 100%, unpinned affordance visible), `board-view-empty`, `board-view-presented` (100%, all tiles unpinned and visibly so), `board-view-zoomed-out` (the zoom-slider payoff: 186 `$board-tile` `mini` instances at a mock-arithmetic 42%, real-world figure ~7.6%, Fit all engaged, edges off, labels hidden, only the 5 pinned markers visible), `board-view-zoomed-in` (200%, one tile, unpinned) for the states from the ticket. Components: `$board-toolbar` (variants `default`/`fitall-edgesoff`/`zoomedin`), `$zoom-slider` (variants `default`/`min`/`max`, range 5–200%), `$pin-button` (variants `default`/`pinned`, inline SVG icon, `default` only shown ≥60% zoom), `$board-tile` (variants `default`/`outside-filter`/`mini`). No new tokens were needed.
